entries.answer: UI/UX Design is for visitors who land on your site or app and leave because they cannot find what they need, or because it looks like it was built years ago. It is the screens, flows, and layout redesigned around what a visitor is actually trying to do, delivered as a clickable Figma design to approve before anything is built. You get every screen mapped to the visitor's goal, and layouts that work on a phone first, then scale up to desktop. Range: $600 to $1,500. What moves the price: number of screens (5 vs 20+), flows, design system.
entries.title: UI/UX Design

entries.answer: Graphics Design is for a business whose posts, ads, and decks all look like they came from different companies. It is a set of designed assets with one consistent look, in the formats needed to use them. You get one consistent look across social, print, and product graphics, and a visual style that still looks like you a year from now. Range: $250 to $800. What moves the price: number of assets (10 vs 40+).
entries.title: Graphics Design

entries.answer: Brand Design is for a new business that needs to look like a real company from day one, or one whose look no longer fits what it sells. It is a logo set, colors, type, and simple usage rules, so anyone can keep the brand consistent. You get a logo set that holds up at any size, from favicon to signage, and colors and type chosen to work together, not picked one by one. Range: $400 to $1,200. What moves the price: logo only vs full identity plus guide.
entries.title: Brand Design

entries.answer: Redesign is for a business with a website or system that looks dated, confuses visitors, or no longer fits, and that wants a fresh makeover without starting from zero. First, a free audit of the site or system (what confuses visitors, what is broken, what is costing inquiries), then a full redesign, new screens and flows, giving it a fresh makeover. You get the free audit report, ranked by impact, new screens and flows, and the redesign handed over ready to build. Range: $800 to $2,500, audit free. What moves the price: pages or screens (5 vs 20+). This replaces the old Design Audit.
entries.title: Redesign

entries.answer: Websites are for a business that is invisible online, or whose site gets visitors but no inquiries. It is a fast site that says what you do in the first screen, with a clear path from visitor to inquiry on every page. You get a site built search-ready, with the titles and descriptions in place. Range: $500 to $2,000. A one-page website starts at $500. What moves the price: pages (1 vs 10+).
entries.title: Websites

entries.answer: Web Apps are for a team doing real work in spreadsheets, chats, and five open tabs. It is a working tool in the browser, a dashboard, a portal, or an internal tool, built around the team's actual workflow, usable on day one, not just looked at. Range: $1,500 to $5,000. What moves the price: features, roles, integrations.
entries.title: Web Apps

entries.answer: Mobile Apps are for a business whose customers live on their phones and need the service in their pocket. It is one Flutter codebase for iOS and Android, designed for one-handed real-life use, app-store-ready. Range: $1,800 to $5,000. What moves the price: features, screens, store setup.
entries.title: Mobile Apps

entries.answer: Systems are for a business where the work lives in people's heads, spreadsheets, and chats, and nothing is in one place. It is one source of truth with the team's workflow built in, handed over with a walkthrough. Range: $1,200 to $4,000. What moves the price: workflows, data, users.
entries.title: Systems

entries.answer: The Lead Capture Agent is for a business losing inquiries between inbox, form, and chat, and only finding out days later. It is an agent that catches every inquiry and puts it in one place, the moment it arrives, each lead logged with where it came from. Range: $400 to $900. One automation starts at $400. What moves the price: channels (1 vs 4+).
entries.title: Lead Capture Agent

entries.answer: The Follow-up Agent is for a business whose leads go cold because no one follows up in time. It is an agent that sends the right follow-up at the right time, and logs every one, so no inquiry goes unanswered. Range: $400 to $900. What moves the price: sequences (1 vs 3+), channels.
entries.title: Follow-up Agent

entries.answer: The Data & Research Agent is for a business that needs a brief on a lead or a market, not a pile of open tabs. It is an agent that gathers the facts that matter for the decision, with sources noted so anything can be checked. Range: $400 to $1,000. What moves the price: sources, depth, frequency.
entries.title: Data & Research Agent

entries.answer: The Reporting Agent is for a business that opens five tools to answer one question. It is a short weekly summary, what happened, what matters, what is next, same shape every week. Range: $400 to $900. What moves the price: reports, data sources, frequency.
entries.title: Reporting Agent

entries.answer: The CRM & Insights Agent is for a business whose records are messy and that cannot see what is falling through. It is an agent that keeps records clean, logs every interaction, and lists what needs a follow-up. Range: $500 to $1,200. What moves the price: records, integrations, insights.
entries.title: CRM & Insights Agent
